title: Your First Weekend at Bates College, Shared as Cards
description: Build a plausible under-21-safe first-weekend sequence, not a ranking. Give each card one role in the sequence and use evergreen places or recurring behaviors rather than one-time events. Be conservative about hours, access, and travel time unless directly sourced.

cards.title: Arrival and Move-In
cards.subtitle: Thursday Morning Kickoff
cards.notes: Arrive at your assigned residence hall to meet your Junior Advisors and Residence Coordinators. Most first-year students move in on the Thursday before classes begin.
cards.short_summary: The official start of the Bates experience begins with move-in day for the incoming class.
cards.evidence_claim: Arrival day for most new students is Thursday, August 27, 2026, as part of the First-Year Experience and New Student Orientation.
cards.access_notes: Access is restricted to incoming students and their families during designated move-in windows.

cards.title: Opening Convocation
cards.subtitle: Formal Academic Welcome
cards.notes: Process across the Historic Quad to Coram Library for the official welcome ceremony. This tradition marks the formal start of your academic journey at Bates.
cards.short_summary: A century-old tradition where the incoming class is formally welcomed to the Bates community on the Historic Quad.
cards.evidence_claim: Opening Convocation is held annually on the terrace of Coram Library, featuring an academic procession across the Historic Quad.
cards.source_title: Opening Convocation at Bates offers timeless and timely advice to the Class of 2028
cards.access_notes: Open to all new students and faculty; typically held outdoors on the Historic Quad.

cards.title: First Meal at Commons
cards.subtitle: Central Dining Hub
cards.notes: Visit the 5-star rated dining hall for your first meal. Remember to sort your waste at the tray window and leave the black mugs inside.
cards.short_summary: The primary dining facility at Bates, known for its centralized 'one-dining-hall' culture.
cards.evidence_claim: The Commons is the main dining hall; weekend brunch and dinner are served until 8:00 PM or 8:30 PM depending on the day.
cards.source_title: Hours of Operation and Meal Prices | Dining, Conferences and Campus Events
cards.access_notes: Requires a Bates ID for entry on the student board plan. Open 7:00 AM to 9:00 PM on weekdays with varying weekend hours.

cards.title: Sunset at Mount David
cards.subtitle: Friday Evening Tradition
cards.notes: Take the short walk up the campus 'mountain' for a panoramic view of Lewiston and the White Mountains. It is a signature spot for first-weekend photos.
cards.short_summary: A rocky outcrop on campus that offers the best views of the surrounding area and is a popular student gathering spot.
cards.evidence_claim: Mount David is a campus landmark where catching a sunset is considered a first-year bucket list item.
cards.source_title: Tick All the Boxes: A Bucket List for Your First Year at Bates
cards.access_notes: Open 24/7; accessible via a short trail behind the Randall Student Center area.

cards.title: Chase Hall After Dark
cards.subtitle: Friday Night Social
cards.notes: Head to Chase Hall for C.H.A.D. events, which include craft nights, bingo, or live performances organized by Campus Activities & Traditions.
cards.short_summary: Weekly Friday night programming designed to provide inclusive, substance-free social options for students.
cards.evidence_claim: Campus Activities & Traditions (CAT) hosts weekly Friday night programming known as Chase Hall After Dark (C.H.A.D.).
cards.access_notes: Events typically start in the evening; check Bates Engage for specific weekly times.

cards.title: Morning Walk at the Puddle
cards.subtitle: Saturday Morning Relaxation
cards.notes: Stroll around 'The Puddle.' While the famous Puddle Jump happens in winter, the lakeside path is a peaceful spot for a Saturday morning walk.
cards.short_summary: The central campus pond, affectionately known as 'The Puddle,' is the site of many Bates traditions.
cards.evidence_claim: Lake Andrews, known as the 'Puddle,' is a central campus feature and the site of the annual Puddle Jump tradition.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor area open 24/7 to the public.

cards.title: Explore the Museum of Art
cards.subtitle: Saturday Afternoon Culture
cards.notes: Visit the Olin Arts Center to see rotating exhibitions. It's a quiet, air-conditioned space to escape the move-in bustle.
cards.short_summary: A teaching museum that brings world-class art and ideas to the Bates campus and Lewiston community.
cards.evidence_claim: The Museum of Art is located in the Olin Arts Center and is open Saturdays from 10:00 AM to 5:00 PM.
cards.source_title: Visit | Museum of Art | Bates College
cards.access_notes: Open Monday-Saturday 10 AM - 5 PM; closed on Sundays.

cards.title: Late Night at the Den
cards.subtitle: Saturday Night Snack
cards.notes: Grab a burger or fries at this alternative dining spot in Chase Hall. It's the go-to place for late-night social interaction and food.
cards.short_summary: A popular retail dining and social space offering a more casual atmosphere than the main Commons.
cards.evidence_claim: The Bobcat Den in Chase Hall offers alternative dining and has recently reintroduced late-night hours.
cards.source_title: First Time in Four Years: Den Opens For Late-Night Option
cards.access_notes: Check current semester schedules for specific late-night hours; typically open until midnight on select nights.

cards.title: Find Your Study Nook
cards.subtitle: Sunday Afternoon Prep
cards.notes: Scope out the floors of Ladd Library to find your preferred study spot before classes start on Monday. The higher the floor, the quieter it gets.
cards.short_summary: The main research library at Bates, providing diverse study spaces and extensive academic resources.
cards.evidence_claim: Ladd Library is open on Sundays from 10:00 AM to 1:00 AM during the regular semester.
cards.access_notes: Bates ID required for access. Open until 1:00 AM on Sunday nights.

cards.title: AESOP Trip Departure
cards.subtitle: Sunday Evening Send-off
cards.notes: Gather on Alumni Walk to meet your student leaders for the Annual Entering Student Outdoor Program (AESOP). These trips are a core orientation experience.
cards.short_summary: A student-led outdoor orientation program that takes first-years on trips across Maine.
cards.evidence_claim: All first-year students participate in AESOP (Annual Entering Student Outdoor Program) during the orientation period.
cards.source_title: Residential Calendar | Residence Life - Bates College
cards.access_notes: Mandatory for first-year students; departure times vary by specific trip assignment.
